title: Unified Evidence Catalog and Delegation Playbook for Hybrid Deployments
author: Imani Rodriguez
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a single, interoperable evidence catalog and delegation model for security, compliance, and incident response across Redwood’s hybrid environments (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private/VPC). It connects RBAC decisions, audit logs, data residency controls, secure SDLC artifacts, and incident evidence packaging into a manageable lifecycle that supports regulatory audits and legal holds without duplicating sensitive telemetry.

Goals and scope:
- Provide a canonical evidence manifest format for incidents, audits, and compliance requests.
- Define delegation boundaries and attestation events for evidence access across teams and tenants.
- Ensure retention, redaction, and cross-border handling rules are applied automatically during evidence assembly.
- Apply to: production hosted API, Redwood Dedicated pools, and customer Private deployments (VPC / on-prem with govnet connectors).

Audience:
- Security & Compliance, SRE, Infra, Product Compliance, Legal, Customer Success, and Engineering teams responsible for packaging evidence for audits or incidents.

Key services referenced:
- redwood-telemetry-collector (RTC): central ingest pipeline for structured telemetry and audit events.
- authz-audit-proxy (AAP): service that enriches auth events with policy context and stores in the audit index.
- evidence-orchestrator (EO): serverless workflow that assembles evidence manifests and performs redaction/archival.
- kms-connector: HSM/KMS bridge used for keying evidence fingerprints and sealed manifests.
- s3-evidence-archive / govnet-archive: storage endpoints used depending on residency policy.

SLOs and thresholds (operational knobs):
- Audit log ingestion: 99.95% of events processed within 30s of generation.
- Evidence manifest assembly: 95% completed within 10 minutes for incidents; 100% within 24 hours for regulatory requests.
- Evidence retrieval API (internal): 99.9% availability, 95th percentile latency < 250ms for small manifests (<= 10 documents).

Canonical evidence manifest (human-readable example):
{
  "manifest_id": "ev-20280202-7a1f",
  "incident_ref": "INC-2028-0123",
  "collected_by": "evidence-orchestrator:v1.4.0",
  "components": ["authz-events", "audit-logs", "kvcache-dumps", "deployment-manifests"],
  "residency": "eu",
  "access_policy": "tiered-legal-approved",
  "sealed_fingerprint": "kms:enc:abcd1234",
  "retention_policy": "evidence-standard-7y"
}

Manifest fields must include service-supplied IDs, timezone-stamped collection windows, and a sealed_fingerprint generated by kms-connector to prove provenance. EO attaches a provenance chain describing each fetch operation and the identity that initiated it (service or human).

RBAC and delegation model (quick reference):
- Roles: security-admin, security-analyst, infra-operator, legal-reviewer, customer-legal-liaison.
- Principle: never give direct S3/govnet storage credentials. All evidence access must be mediated by EO and gated by an access_policy.
- Short-lived delegation (JIT): EO issues timebound tokens (max 4 hours) for authorized downloads; tokens require a 2-person attestation for sensitive manifests (label contains "sensitive-pii").

Audit logging requirements for evidence-grade events:
- Required event types: authorization_grant, authorization_deny, role_change, api_key_issue, api_key_revoke, evidence_manifest_create, evidence_manifest_access, log_export_request.
- Each event must include: actor_id, actor_type, target_resource, policy_version, request_id, correlation_id, timestamp_utc, and residency_tag.
- Example enrichment query (CLI):
  curl -G https://telemetry.redwood.internal/v1/query --data-urlencode "q=event_type:evidence_manifest_create AND timestamp:[now-1h TO now]" --header "Authorization: Bearer $RTK"

Data residency and retention matrix (short):
| Evidence type | Geolocation default | Archive target | Min retention | Redaction rule |
|---------------|---------------------|----------------|---------------|----------------|
| Audit logs | region-of-origin | s3-evidence-archive / govnet-archive | 7 years | none (indexed) |
| Authz events | region-of-origin | s3-evidence-archive | 3 years | mask user.email for third-party exports |
| Deployment manifests | origin region | govnet-archive (if private) | 7 years | redact secrets, keep checksums |
| PII attachments | customer-region | govnet-archive | regulatory-minimum (customer-specific) | redact all but hashed identifier |

NOTE: table above is normative; EO enforces routing using the residency tag on every manifest and will fail the assembly if a mismatch is detected.

Secure SDLC artifact linkage:
- SDLC artifacts required to support evidence requests: build checksums, SBOM for deployed model binaries, pipeline run IDs, security-scan reports (SAST/DAST), and deployment approval records.
- Artifact storage: signed SBOMs are uploaded to s3-sbom-store and referenced by manifest checksums. EO will fetch those artifacts as part of manifest assembly.

Incident response evidence assembly workflow (step-by-step):
1) Triage: Incident owner opens INC-* ticket and sets evidence_requirements label (low/medium/high).
2) Create manifest: On triage owner approval, EO starts a manifest with artifact list (automated) and marks residency.
3) Obtain delegation: EO requests JIT tokens for retrieval; security-admin must approve for high sensitivity.
4) Redaction pass: EO runs configured redaction rules (PII masking, secret scrub). Redaction report saved alongside manifest.
5) Seal and store: EO invokes kms-connector to produce sealed_fingerprint and uploads to the correct archive endpoint.
6) Notification & access: EO notifies stakeholders with a signed link; access requires 2FA and attestation for sensitive cases.

Numbered runbook for urgent legal hold (24-hour target):
1. Legal files request ticket and tags incident as "legal-hold".
2. Security-ops runs: 
   - ./eoctl hold --incident INC-YYYY --scope full --notify security-ops@example.com
   - EO returns manifest_id; confirm sealed_fingerprint exists.
3. Infra toggles retention lock on the archive object (governed API): 
   - aws s3api put-object-retention --bucket evidence-bucket --key ev-2028/... --retention "{\"Mode\":\"GOVERNANCE\",\"RetainUntilDate\":\"2035-02-02T00:00:00Z\"}"
4. Legal and Security verify via EO signed proof and attach to matter tracking system.

Compliance evidence packaging checklist (before handoff):
- [ ] Manifest includes sealed_fingerprint and provenance chain.
- [ ] All artifacts have checksums and storage URIs.
- [ ] Redaction report appended.
- [ ] Delegation logs (who accessed what and when) included.
- [ ] Residency tags validated and archive endpoint confirmed.

Risk and exceptions handling:
- Exceptions (e.g., short retention requested by customer or emergency cross-region export) must be recorded in the authorization-exceptions register with: approver, rationale, compensating controls, and expiration.
- Emergency cross-border export: must include a temporary extra audit stream to the legal-audit index and an oncall attestation recorded in the manifest.

Evidence QA and sampling:
- Quarterly sampling: security will run a blind re-assembly of 5% of manifests to validate redaction and provenance.
- Metric: target <1% sampling failures; if exceeded, elevated review and rolling remediation plan.

Appendix A — Example EO CLI commands and JSON outputs:
- Create manifest (simulated):
  eoctl create --incident INC-2028-0123 --residency eu --components authz,audit,deploy 
  => {"manifest_id": "ev-20280202-7a1f", "status": "in-progress"}

- Seal and upload (simulated):
  eoctl seal --manifest ev-20280202-7a1f --kms-key alias/evidence-key 
  => {"manifest_id": "ev-20280202-7a1f", "sealed_fingerprint": "kms:enc:abcd1234", "archive_uri": "s3://s3-evidence-archive/evidence/ev-20280202-7a1f"}

Appendix B — Owner matrix:
- Evidence orchestration (EO): ownership: security-ops; primary contact: security-ops@example.com
- Audit ingestion (RTC): ownership: infra-observability; primary contact: telemetry@example.com
- Authz enrichment (AAP): ownership: auth-platform; primary contact: auth-platform@example.com
- Legal hold and escalations: ownership: legal; primary contact: legal-compliance@example.com

- Authorization change control: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/authorization-change-control-and-evidence-playbook-2025
- SDLC artifact policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/secure-sdlc/sdlc-security-gates-rbac-audit-residency-checklist-2026

Maintenance and review cadence:
- This playbook is reviewed semi-annually by Security, Infra, and Legal. Emergency updates occur after any material incident affecting evidence integrity.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: security-ops@example.com (pager: +1-555-EO-OPS)
- Legal escalation: legal-compliance@example.com

End of document.
